title: eVir network model identifies repurposed oral drugs active against SARS-CoV-2
summary: The eVir pipeline uses Node2Vec embeddings of drug-protein and protein-protein networks with a Siamese network and MLPs to rank drugs by similarity to antiviral peptides. Compounds including mebendazole, gefitinib and topotecan were tested in SARS-CoV-2-infected Calu-3 cells and a lead compound in K18-hACE2 mice. The similarity model reported accuracy 97.28% and AUC 99.47%, a similarity task rather than antiviral efficacy.
ai_technology: Node2Vec graph embeddings feeding a Siamese network and MLPs to score drug similarity to antiviral peptides

evidence.tested: Experimental testing of selected compounds in infected cells and mice.
evidence.unknown: Quantitative antiviral potency and mouse outcomes are not given in the abstract; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Ranked existing drugs for antiviral repurposing.
